45308-the-adventure-girls-in-the-air.title: In The Air
45308-the-adventure-girls-in-the-air.creator: Unknown
45308-the-adventure-girls-in-the-air.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. three boys present agreed heartily with her. The plane, its engine roaring, dove straight for the blue waters of the Atlantic, only to zoom upward again when the waves threatened to engulf it. The young people, when nothing happened, turned their attention to something else. Airplanes were familiar to them. “How did you make out in your English exam today?” Carol asked her friend, Janet Gordon. The girl in the bright red bathing suit made a wry face and sighed.

arxiv-1703-02504.title: Leveraging Large Amounts of Weakly Supervised Data for Multi-Language Sentiment Classification Conference: WWW 2017, April 3–7, 2017, Perth, Australia.
arxiv-1703-02504.creator: Jan Deriu Aurelien Lucchi Valeria De Luca, Aliaksei Severyn Simon Müller Mark Cieliebak, Thomas Hofmann Martin Jaggi
arxiv-1703-02504.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel approach for multi-lingual sentiment classification in short texts. This is a challenging task as the amount of training data in languages other than English is very limited. Previously proposed multi-lingual approaches typically require to establish a correspondence to English for which powerful classifiers are already available.

arxiv-2101-12500.title: Nuclear Quantum Effects on Autoionization of Water Isotopologues Studied by Ab Initio Path Integral Molecular Dynamics
arxiv-2101-12500.creator: Bo Thomsen, Motoyuki Shiga
arxiv-2101-12500.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bo Thomsen, Motoyuki Shiga. In this study we investigate the nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) on the acidity constant (p K A K_{A} ) of liquid water isotopologues at the ambient condition by path integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) simulations. We compared simulations using a fully explicit solvent model with a classical polarizable force field, density functional tight binding, and ab initio density functional theory, which correspond to empirical, semiempirical, and ab initio PIMD simulations, respectively.

arxiv-2103-09483.title: Modeling of chemically active particles at an air-liquid interface
arxiv-2103-09483.creator: Shun Imamura 1,2, Toshihiro Kawakatsu 1
arxiv-2103-09483.description: Abstract The collective motion of chemically active particles at an air-liquid interface is studied theoretically as a dynamic self-organization problem. Based on a physical consideration, we propose a minimal model for self-propelled particles by combining hydrodynamic interaction, capillary interaction, driving force by Marangoni effect, and Marangoni flow.

arxiv-2104-10002.title: A revisit of symmetry analysis and group classifications of Boiti–Leon–Pempinelli system in (2+1)-dimensions
arxiv-2104-10002.creator: Manjit Singh
arxiv-2104-10002.description: Abstract In this paper, the Boiti–Leon–Pempinelli system in (2+1)-dimensions is revisited for Lie symmetries and invariant solutions. An infinite dimensional Lie algebra is obtained using the Lie invariance criterion and is further classified into one, two and three-dimensional optimal list of subalgebra. We obtain new explicit exact solutions involving arbitrary functions that have never been documented in previous work.

arxiv-2108-13634.title: Sea urchin sperm exploit extremum seeking control to find the egg
arxiv-2108-13634.creator: Mahmoud Abdelgalil, Yasser Aboelkassem, Haithem Taha
arxiv-2108-13634.description: Abstract Sperm cells perform extremely demanding tasks with minimal capabilities. The cells must quickly navigate in a noisy environment to find an egg within a short time window for successful fertilization without any global positioning information. Many research efforts have been dedicated to derive mathematical principles that explain their superb navigation strategy.

arxiv-2205-05921.title: 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 resonant superalgebra for supergravity
arxiv-2205-05921.creator: Remigiusz Durka, Krzysztof M. Graczyk
arxiv-2205-05921.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Remigiusz Durka, Krzysztof M. Graczyk. We present new superalgebra for 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 D = 3 , 4 D=3,4 supergravity theory endowed with the U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) generator. The superalgebra is rooted in the so-called Soroka-Soroka algebra and spanned by the Lorentz J a ​ b J_{ab} and Lorentz-like Z a ​ b Z_{ab} , translation P a P_{a} and T T generators, as well as two supercharges Q α I Q^{I}_{\alpha} .

arxiv-2311-04230.title: Stringlet Excitation Model of the Boson Peak
arxiv-2311-04230.creator: Cunyuan Jiang, Matteo Baggioli, Jack F. Douglas
arxiv-2311-04230.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cunyuan Jiang, Matteo Baggioli, Jack F. Douglas. The boson peak (BP), a low-energy excess in the vibrational density of states over the Debye contribution, is often identified as a characteristic of amorphous solid materials. Despite decades of efforts, its microscopic origin still remains a mystery. Recently, it has been proposed, and corroborated with simulations, that the BP might stem from intrinsic localized modes involving one-dimensional (1D) string-like excitations (“stringlets”).

arxiv-2507-21724.title: Agent-Based Exploration of Recommendation Systems in Misinformation Propagation
arxiv-2507-21724.creator: Lise Jakobsen, Anna Johanne Holden Jacobsen, Önder Gürcan, Özlem Özgöbek
arxiv-2507-21724.description: Abstract This study uses agent-based modeling to examine the impact of various recommendation algorithms on the propagation of misinformation on online social networks. We simulate a synthetic environment consisting of heterogeneous agents, including regular users, bots, and influencers, interacting through a social network with recommendation systems.

arxiv-2508-03468.creator: Guido Alex Iandolo, Alex Amato, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Alessandro Delmonte, Jan-Simon Hennig, Margot Hennig, Sebastian Steinlechner, Janis Wöhler, Stefan Hild, Jessica Steinlechner

The next generation of gravitational-wave detectors, such as the Einstein Telescope, is designed to reduce noise in a wide band of frequencies compared to the current generation, through the use of new technologies. ETpathfinder, designed as an R&D facility for these technologies, is a prototype for which the mirrors were chosen to be made of crystalline silicon, produced by the Leibniz-Institut für Kristallzüchtung.

pmc-11421477.title: Discovering the anti-diabetic potential of pomegranate peel metabolites by examining molecular interplay with the thioredoxin-interacting protein
pmc-11421477.creator: Tahira Aslam, Amina Arif, Shafia Arshad, Fatima Muccee, Khalil Ahmad, Muhammad Omer Iqbal, Umair Khalil, Suhail Razak, Tayyaba Afsar, Ali Almajwal, Huma Shafique, Maryam Zain
pmc-11421477.description: IntroductionMedicinal plants like Punica granatum (pomegranate) have traditional uses against diabetes, inflammation and other diseases. The study was initiated to get an insight into the interaction tendency of P. granatum derived compounds with diabetes associated human thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP). High glucose in diabetes induces production of TXNIP resulting in β-cells apoptosis. Its inhibition might reduce the diabetes incidence.

pmc-11432028.title: Special Survival Strategy of First-Instar Scorpions Revealed by Synchronous Molting Behavior from Social Facilitation of Maternal Care and Reciprocal Aggregation
pmc-11432028.creator: Yiyuan Guo, Songryong Li, Sijia Lu, Xinrong Wang, Zhijian Cao, Yingliang Wu
pmc-11432028.description: Simple SummaryThe ecdysis of arthropods is an essential process for survival, growth, and reproduction. Independent molting behavior is widely adopted by most arthropods, but synchronous molting behavior is uncommon in some groups of arthropods. Synchronous molting behavior is sometimes caused by stimuli from the physical environment and food supply and sometimes involves social facilitation.

pmc-12613730.title: Do immune system and microbiome–gut–brain axis interactions associate with major depressive disorder?
pmc-12613730.creator: Hui Zhao, Larissa Tao, Cheng Tang, Wa Cai, Weidong Shen
pmc-12613730.description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading psychiatric disorder with increasing global prevalence, yet its underlying pathogenesis remains inadequately elucidated. Increasing evidence highlights the complex interplay between the immune system, gut microbiota, and their bidirectional crosstalk with the central nervous system. Gut microbiota dysbiosis affects neuroimmune and intestinal immune homeostasis, driving bidirectional peripheral-central immune responses through immune-to-brain and gut-to-brain communication.

pmc-13038899.description: IntroductionHericenone C exhibits antinociceptive effects in inflammatory pain; however, its molecular target and underlying mechanism remain unclear.Methods and ResultsWe assessed the effect of hericenone C on formalin-induced nociceptive behavior in mice and explored its molecular target using in vitro experiments.

pmc-13206809.title: Recurrent Pericarditis in a Middle-Aged Female with MEFV Mutation
pmc-13206809.creator: Xiaohang Liu, Tongxin Xiao, Lihua Zhang, Zhongjie Fan, Xinglin Yang, Zhuang Tian
pmc-13206809.description: Recurrent pericarditis (RP) remains challenging, especially in tuberculosis (TB)-endemic regions where empirical anti-TB therapy is often unnecessarily prolonged. We report a 35-year-old woman with three RP episodes over six months, presenting with pleuritic chest pain, elevated inflammatory markers, and moderate-to-large pericardial effusion. Extensive infectious (including TB), autoimmune, and malignancy workups were negative.

pmc-13597183.title: Effects of kudzu extract on alcohol consumption among men and women seeking treatment for alcohol use disorder
pmc-13597183.creator: Diana R Keith, Jing Liu, Gordana Vitaliano, Scott E Lukas
pmc-13597183.description: BackgroundWe previously demonstrated that standardized kudzu extract (NPI-031) reduced drinking in a four-week trial among non-treatment-seeking men diagnosed with alcohol abuse or dependence. The present study assessed the safety and efficacy of eight weeks of kudzu among treatment-seeking men and women with alcohol use disorder (AUD).

uslaw-usc-t49-s60130.title: 49 U.S.C. § 60130 — Pipeline safety information grants to communities
uslaw-usc-t49-s60130.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s60130.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Chapter 601 (Safety). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Grant Authority.— (1) In general.— The Secretary of Transportation may make grants for technical assistance to local communities, Indian Tribes, and groups of individuals (not including for-profit entities) relating to the safety of pipeline facilities in local communities, other than facilities regulated under Public Law 93–153 (43.
